title: Large-scale embedding ingest: async batch API, streaming partial-results, and idempotency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a scalable embedding ingestion surface that supports: (1) a transactional async batch job API for very large datasets, (2) streaming partial-results for low-latency consumption of earliest batches, and (3) robust idempotency and retry semantics for customer-facing SDKs and internal workers. This will improve throughput for high-volume customers, reduce p99 latency for initial results, and provide deterministic retries for duplicate-safe pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/embeddings/ingest creates an async job and returns a job_id with input_summary
Streaming: GET /v1/embeddings/ingest/{job_id}/stream provides SSE/HTTP chunked partial batches as they complete
Idempotency: client-provided idempotency_key or generated job fingerprint prevents double-processing across retries
Retries: server-side resumable workers can safely resume jobs using persisted checkpoints without duplication
Scale: system can sustain 2M documents/day across a single deployment with configurable shard parallelism
Observability: job-level metrics (enqueue_time, processing_rate, failures_count) and per-batch latency histograms are visible in Console
Backwards compatibility: existing single-request embeddings endpoints remain unchanged; SDKs opt-in to batch API
technical_details: Design uses a two-phase pipeline: upload & validate -> schedule compute shards -> compute & persist embeddings -> index/forward to downstream stores. Clients may upload NDJSON or compressed archive (gzip/.tar.gz). Server creates a Job record with metadata: input_uri(s), idempotency_key, desired_batch_size, model, quantization_profile, priority. Workers pick up job shards from a durable JobQueue (Postgres + partitioned Kafka topic). Each shard checkpoint is persisted to enable exactly-once semantics: worker writes per-item fingerprint into a dedupe table with idempotency_key+item_hash and only writes embeddings if insertion succeeds. For large jobs we stream partial results via SSE or websocket by pushing completed shard batches to a streaming topic; the ingest API returns both job_id and a streaming_url. Retries: client retries with same idempotency_key; server deduplicates on Job creation and on per-item writes. Idempotency_key TTL configurable (default 30 days).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): API + job metadata schema, Postgres Job table, simple worker that handles small NDJSON uploads synchronously fallback
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Durable queue integration (Kafka), shard scheduler, worker checkpoint writes and per-item dedupe table
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Streaming partial results (SSE), Console integration for job view and metrics
Phase 4 (1 week): SDK updates for Python/Node: upload helpers, idempotency_key generation, streaming client examples
Phase 5 (1 week): Load testing, chaos testing (worker restarts, partial failures), and rollout in Canary orgs
Phase 6 (ongoing): Gradual ramp to GA, add storage connectors (S3, GCS) and archive ingestion
requests_and_endpoints: POST /v1/embeddings/ingest -> { job_id, status: queued, streaming_url, input_summary }
GET /v1/embeddings/ingest/{job_id}/stream -> SSE stream of {batch_id, records_processed, partial_results_url} or chunked NDJSON
POST /v1/embeddings/ingest/{job_id}/cancel -> cancels remaining shards and marks job
data_contracts: Input NDJSON line schema: {"id": string, "text": string, "metadata": optional object } - each line treated as one item
Response batch schema: {batch_id, items: [{id, status, embedding_ref_or_error}]}
Checkpoint schema: {job_id, shard_id, last_processed_index, processed_count, updated_at}
scaling_strategy: Shard jobs by (job_id % N_shards) and by file byte ranges for uploads larger than 64MB. Autoscale worker pools based on queue lag and per-shard processing latency. Use adaptive batch sizing: start with configured batch_size and increase if latency SLOs permit to improve throughput. For multi-tenant isolation, assign hot tenants to reserved worker pools or apply fair-queuing and token-bucket rate limits.
testing_plan: Unit tests for job lifecycle state transitions and idempotency path
Integration tests: end-to-end NDJSON upload -> full job completion with partial stream consumption
Load tests: simulate 100 concurrent large jobs with 100k items each; validate throughput, memory, and dedupe correctness
Chaos tests: worker preemption, Kafka partition loss, DB failover; verify resume behavior
Property tests: random duplicate item replays produce identical final outputs
monitoring_and_slos: Track job_accept_latency < 1s median, first_batch_latency p50 < 2s for small jobs, per-item p99 processing latency target 500ms for optimized kernels. Alert on queue_lag > threshold, dedupe_table_write_errors > 0.5% and sustained worker restarts. Expose metrics to Console and add log links for failed items.
rollout_plan: Canary with three existing SMB customers and internal corp accounts for 2 weeks. Expose feature flag per-org to opt-in SDK behavior. After 2 weeks of stability and no major regressions, flip default for accounts created after rollout date and communicate migration guide.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: dedupe table could grow large and slow inserts -> Mitigation: TTL + periodic compaction and partitioning by month
Risk: partially-processed jobs cause customer confusion -> Mitigation: clear job states (paused/failed/complete) and tools to resume/cancel; streaming provides early visibility
Risk: expensive replay of large jobs on accidental duplicates -> Mitigation: enforce idempotency_key at create-time and reject duplicates, plus soft-warnings on suspected duplicate inputs
Risk: increased operational cost due to storage for intermediate batches -> Mitigation: compressed batch payloads and configurable retention policy per job
notes: We should coordinate with Platform SRE for Kafka partitions and with Security for storage encryption of intermediate upload payloads. Consider a lightweight server-side checksum to validate client uploads and to seed item_hash for dedupe. Explore offering a low-cost 'ingest-only' SLA with longer completion windows for archival customers.
